title: Connect, change, check, repair or disconnect a GitLab connection
description: POST /api/v1/integrations/gitlab sends connect, replace, check or repair; DELETE sends disconnect. The token travels only in connect and replace, goes once to the mapped daemon, which validates it against the base's /user, /personal_access_tokens/self and one page of the person's projects and writes it into glab's own config.yml host entry, and is never returned, logged or kept anywhere else. connect infers https:// only when no scheme is given and never corrects a host; gitlab.com and a self-hosted GitLab (with an explicit port or a relative-URL base path) are the same form. glab keeps one account per server, so a connect to a server glab already holds a login for is refused. connection_id is one the daemon derived from glab's file; it selects nothing else. check reads GitLab now; the list never touches the network. repair registers the secretless Git credential helper for the connection's base again. disconnect logs glab's entry out as glab auth logout does: it revokes nothing at GitLab and leaves every clone in place, and it is refused while one of this daemon's clones uses the connection.

token.description: A GitLab personal, group, project or fine-grained access token: printable ASCII without spaces. read_api and write_repository are the scopes the form asks for; api also works.
